Extremely Disappointing Experience – Food Safety Ignored & Unprofessional Behaviour
This was my first and last experience with this restaurant, and unfortunately, it has been deeply disturbing—not just because of the food issue but because of how the staff and social media team handled it.
I ordered Davanagere Benne Masala Dosa from the Malad West outlet and found hard, crystal/plastic-like foreign particles inside the food while eating. This is a serious food safety and hygiene violation, not a minor complaint.
When I contacted the restaurant, one of the staff members assured me that they would help and specifically guided me to approach Zomato and also email them, stating that this was the correct process. I followed their instructions exactly. However, Zomato outright refused to help or issue a refund, despite clear photographic evidence.
What is truly shocking is what followed next.
When I went back to the restaurant team and their social media handles for support, instead of standing by their words or taking responsibility, they completely changed their attitude.
My comments explaining the issue were deleted from their social media pages
Messages were left unanswered
There was no follow-up, no accountability, and no resolution
This behaviour feels like a deliberate attempt to silence genuine complaints rather than address a serious concern. Saying “we are here to help” and then deleting comments and ignoring the customer is highly unprofessional, unethical, and misleading.
If this is how a restaurant reacts to a food contamination issue, it raises serious questions about their internal standards and customer ethics. Customers are not asking for favours—we are asking for basic food safety and honest accountability.
I am extremely disappointed with the staff’s behaviour and the way the social media team handled this matter. This review is being posted so other customers are aware of how genuine issues are treated once money has already been taken.
Food quality, customer trust, and transparency clearly need urgent attention here.

This matter has been reviewed and addressed multiple times by our team.

We had clearly and explicitly conveyed our willingness to approve the refund immediately upon receiving the official intimation from Zomato. However, to date, no such intimation has been received by us.
As part of our standard food-safety and quality-assurance procedures, we requested verification of the alleged foreign object. This request was declined from your end, making it impossible for us to validate the claim or initiate any corrective action.
Despite repeated communication and clear guidance on the appropriate resolution process, the matter has instead been escalated publicly across social media and review platforms. Such actions do not enable a fair, factual, or verifiable resolution.
We reiterate that we remain open to resolving this matter strictly through the appropriate and verifiable channel. Any further public allegations made without substantiation or cooperation will be duly noted.
We remain fully committed to hygiene, quality, and fair resolution for all our customers—something that is consistently reflected in our long-standing reputation and customer feedback to date.

Team,
Shree Gomateshwara Bhavan

featured_reviews.review_text:
For anyone who enjoys authentic south indian food, this is an okay place. Fair warning: food is strictly vegetarian.

Special thanks to our hosts for the evening Ms. Shivani and Mr. Raj for their hospitality. They helped us understand and pick dishes from the menu.

Kamat's Legacy serves unlimited Thali for lunch/dinner/breakfast. I tried the unlimited Thali for dinner but sadly it's not at par with other unlimited thali options that I have tried. The food is served hot and fresh but the amount and variety of dishes in are severely limited. Just about 4-5 dishes which includes the curries, no sambar or rasam are included which is really odd and the cost of this thali is ₹550 which is not justified.

Then comes the service: usually places offering unlimited thali (such as Maharaja Bhog or Jain Sabkuch) have an entire entourage of multiple servers constantly refilling your food without having to ask. There is no such system here. You have to request for refill every time and each time it takes them up to 5-10 minutes to get your dishes which breaks the tempo of eating.

I would rather prefer Jain Sabkuch or Maharajag Bhog if I really want to try the unlimited veg thali experience. Their service is top notch and the variety/amount of dishes offered is also better and at the same price as the unlimited thali served here.

We also ordered Bisi Bheli Bhaat and Podi Idli apart from the thali which were also disappointing. The quantity of food being served for the a la carte dishes doesn't justify the price of those items. For Podi Idli, we only got 3 medium sized idlis.

The quantity and quality of the food versus the price was a letdown which is why I don't really recommend this place that much. I also don't understand why there is an additional "service charge" included in our bill which is additional to the GST and CGST which we are already paying.

The only redeeming quality of our experience was the assortment of chutneys and pickles which is why I give it at least 2 stars.

featured_reviews.name: Kuldip Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌿 Banana Leaf – A Slice of South India in Malad 🌿

If you’re looking for authentic South Indian vegetarian cuisine, Banana Leaf is easily one of the best in Malad. This place celebrates the flavors of the South with a menu that spans specialties from Andhra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka — bringing the diversity of Southern kitchens onto your plate.

The variety is impressive: from crisp dosas, fluffy idlis, crunchy vadas, and hearty uttapams to full traditional meals. The highlight for me was their Dakshin Bhojanam Thali — a wholesome spread of curries paired with appam or parotta, with a choice of bisi bele bhath or steamed rice. Each bite was a journey through authentic regional flavors.

We also tried the Rasam Vada, and I must say — the rasam was outstanding. Honestly, I’d visit again just for that comforting, tangy-soulful bowl.

The ambience is cozy and minimalistic, enhanced by soft South Indian instrumental music and staff dressed in traditional attire — little touches that complete the cultural vibe. The service is warm, cordial, and attentive, making the whole experience even better.

💡 Verdict: A must-visit if you’re craving South Indian food — wholesome, authentic, and full of flavor. 🍛✨

featured_reviews.name: The Lucky Guide
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was browsing through the nearby restaurants available to try something different and this place stood out by offering Tamilnadu cuisine, though after seeing a few photos on Google I understood that this is not the place I would want to sit and eat so I rather do a take out.

I arrive at the restaurant within a 7-8 minute walk, it is located at the end if Gautam Buddh road after 2-3 shops towards the left in a small lane that leads towards link road.

There were 2 tables that were occupied, I ask the guy at the counter for a menu and browsed to notice Indian cuisine, a few Tamilnadu cuisines and Chinese cuisine, since I am still trying to find a restaurant that serves the right biryani I thought let's try the biryani out here as it said Tamilnadu style. Additionally I ordered a chicken 65 again Tamilnadu style.

Whilst waiting for the order, I asked if they had a take away menu to which he replied that the prices on that menu are old as they have now increased the prices on the new menu however all items are available and they do home delivery by charging what Dunzo charges them, which sounded pretty acceptable, in the mean time I observed the restaurant, it's a small decent place, looked clean from where I was waiting, now keep in mind this place is good for bachelor's only, I definitely do not recommend girls, women or families visiting.

The order was picked up within 10 minutes coz they weren't busy and I walk back home.

Let's talk about the food. I ate similar biryani when I was in Hyderabad, they don't serve a biryani masala like how the other typical one's are available out there, it was biryani flavored rice with one big piece of chicken leg, egg curry, onion raita, and a pappad.

The chicken 65 was masala coated red color deep fried chicken, Ike a dry snack, more like and South Indian boneless chicken lollipop.

The biryani rice was under cooked, could have been cooked for maybe 3-4 minutes more or maybe kept on dum to be perfectly cooked, the taste was definitely tamilian and it made me get the feeling of being in South India. I didn't get to taste the egg curry coz the biryani was so much that I couldn't eat anything more, I loved the onion raita and the big sized pappad. Overall I was more than jus satisfied with what was served.

To beat it all the biryani costed 140/- & the chicken 65 costed 100/-, believe me when I tell you this place lived up to all expectations after paying so less, and I must say they are doing a fabulous job catering to all those people who want to eat some good food & yet pocket friendly.

So all you people out there who are looking for a pocket friendly restaurant, you people must try this place coz I say it's more than worthit for the price you pay.

featured_reviews.name: Kiyansh Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
With multiple popular branches spread across Mumbai—including Kandivali West (Mahavir Nagar), Borivali West, Mira Road, Malad, and several Andheri Metro stations—South Tiffin House has carved out a solid niche for itself. It positions itself as an affordable, fast-casual quick service brand.
Depending on the outlet you visit, the setup ranges from small, cozy indoor seating spaces to minimalist, metro-station grab-and-go counters. It is designed for quick meals, casual weekend breakfasts, or late-night street food cravings.
The Food: Traditional Roots Meet Fusion Twists
The menu is a massive playground that balances classic Udupi-style staples with experimental fusion items that cater heavily to Mumbai’s street food culture.
The Must-Try Classics:
The undisputed crowd-pleasers here are the Thatte Idlis. They are large, plate-sized, pillowy-soft Karnataka-style idlis. Getting them as the Ghee Podi Thatte Idli is highly recommended; the generous dousing of aromatic ghee and flavorful gun powder (podi) is incredibly satisfying. Their classic Mysore Masala Dosa and crispy Medu Vada are also solid, reliable picks.
The Fusion Experiments:
If you like adventurous street food flavors, they offer unique options like Sri Lankan Curry Paniyaram, Peri Peri Mini Idlis, and Pizza Uttapams. The Sri Lankan style dishes featuring rich coconut-milk based flavors are a pleasant surprise for a fast-casual menu.
Filter Coffee:
No South Indian meal is complete without it, and their strong, aromatic filter coffee serves as the perfect finishing touch.
Areas for Improvement
While the food taste is generally well-received and offers great value for money, consistency can vary across branches and platforms:
In-House vs. Delivery: Diners frequently note that eating fresh, piping-hot food at the restaurant is a far superior experience. On delivery apps, the sambhar and chutneys can occasionally arrive running a bit cold or watery, and crispy dosas inevitably soften in transit.
The Sambhar Dynamic: If you prefer highly authentic, deeply traditional, tangy Tamil-style sambhar, you might find their version leans slightly on the sweeter side to match local Mumbai preferences.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered the Misal from South Tiffin House through

Zomato after reading a few good reviews, but it turned out to be quite disappointing. The Misal was extremely oily, and the excess oil completely overpowered the flavor of the dish. Instead of getting that nice balance of spice and tang that makes Misal enjoyable, it just tasted greasy and

heavy.

The farsan portion was another letdown. It was very little, almost like they forgot it's supposed to be an essential part of the dish. Without enough farsan, the Misal lost its crunch and texture, which made it feel incomplete. The pav was fine and the packaging was decent, but the main dish itself just didn't deliver.

I had higher expectations from South Tiffin House, especially since they're known for traditional snacks. With a few improvements, this could actually be a good Misal. If they reduce the oil and serve a more generous amount of farsan, the taste would improve a lot. Right now though, I wouldn't recommend ordering it if you're looking for an authentic, well-balanced Misal. I hope they work on this because the potential is definitely there, but the current version just misses the mark.
